img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: Many Ravenswood buildings have enclosed back porches where laundry or a utility sink was added later. Those rooms are rarely heated as well as the main house. On a subzero night, the pipes there are the first to freeze. Insulating them, adding a small heat source and shutting off and draining lines you don't use in winter can prevent the most common burst pipe we see here.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From Ravenswood Homeowners

items.q: My back porch pipes froze. What should I do?
items.preview: Shut off the line if you can and call us.
items.answer: If there's a shutoff for that line, close it. Don't use an open flame to thaw. Call us.

items.q: How do I keep pipes from freezing?
items.preview: Heat, open cabinets and a slow drip.
items.answer: Keep the heat up, open cabinets on exterior walls and let a faucet drip on the coldest nights.

items.q: Can you repair pipe inside a plaster wall?
items.answer: Yes. We locate the break and open only what's needed.

items.q: Should I shut off porch pipes for the winter?
items.preview: If you don't use them, yes.
items.answer: If you don't need them in winter, shut them off and drain them.

items.q: How much does burst pipe repair cost in Ravenswood?
items.preview: It depends on the break. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the pipe burst and how we reach it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
